intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM — collect luggage, pick up a lei greeting if available at the terminal, and arrange ground transportation to your accommodation. Take time to freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby local beach for a relaxed first afternoon. Waikiki Beach (if on Oahu) is walkable from many budget hotels and free to access. Enjoy the warm sand, gentle waves, and stunning Pacific views. Rent a bodyboard from a local vendor for around $10/hour for family fun.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront promenade at sunset. Visit a nearby ABC Store or local grocery (Times Supermarket) to stock up on snacks and drinks for the trip to save on meal costs throughout the week.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at the airport — look for local plate lunch counters or a convenience store for a budget-friendly snack under $8.
meals.lunch: Pick up a plate lunch from a local food truck or deli near the beach — try a classic Hawaiian plate with rice, macaroni salad, and teriyaki chicken for around $10–$12.
meals.dinner: Visit a local grocery store deli or a budget-friendly spot like L&L Hawaiian Barbecue for a filling dinner under $15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the late morning arrival. Focus on settling in, resting, and getting your bearings. Keep receipts and set a daily spending target of around $50–$70 per adult to stay on budget.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (Oahu) — a iconic and affordable hike ($5/person entry fee) offering panoramic views of Honolulu and the coastline. Start early (7–8 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. The trail is about 1.6 miles round trip and family-friendly for older kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for snorkeling — one of Hawaii's best free-to-low-cost snorkeling spots ($25/adult, children under 12 free). Rent snorkel gear on-site for around $12. Watch the mandatory marine education video and explore the vibrant reef teeming with tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area and explore a local neighborhood for dinner. Walk along Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki for people-watching and street entertainment, which is completely free.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at the hotel using groceries purchased the night before — fruit, granola bars, and juice to save money.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from the grocery store to enjoy at Hanauma Bay's picnic area — saves $15–$20 compared to buying food on-site.
meals.dinner: Try Ono Seafood or a similar local poke shop for fresh, affordable Hawaiian poke bowls at around $12–$15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Hanauma Bay reservations online in advance — entry is limited and slots fill up fast, especially in August. Bring reef-safe sunscreen (required by Hawaii law). August weather may bring occasional rain showers; pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the North Shore of Oahu — take a scenic drive or public bus (TheBus route is very affordable at $3/ride) to Haleiwa Town. Browse the charming surf shops, local art galleries, and historic buildings. Visit Waimea Valley for a nature walk ($20/adult, $10 children) leading to a beautiful waterfall and botanical garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Sunset Beach or Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline) — both are free public beaches with stunning scenery. In August, waves are calmer and ideal for swimming with kids. Look for sea turtles resting on the sand (keep a respectful distance).
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa — a legendary North Shore institution serving garlic shrimp plates for around $14. Enjoy your meal at picnic tables under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Grab a malasada (Portuguese doughnut) from Leonard's Bakery or a local bakery on the way — a beloved Hawaii treat at about $1.50 each.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the beach, or grab a shave ice from Matsumoto Shave Ice in Haleiwa for a refreshing treat at $4–$6.
meals.dinner: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck — garlic shrimp plate with rice for around $14 per person. A true North Shore bucket-list experience.

day_by_day.notes: TheBus is the most budget-friendly way to get around Oahu — a day pass costs $7.50. If renting a car, gas and parking add up; compare costs. North Shore is about 45 minutes from Waikiki by car. Bring water shoes for Waimea Valley's waterfall swim.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant site. The basic grounds and memorials are free to walk; the USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is also free (timed passes required, book online in advance). Arrive early as passes go quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Battleship Missouri Memorial ($32/adult, $16 children) or the Pacific Aviation Museum ($25/adult, $15 children) if budget allows — both are on Ford Island and offer fascinating family-friendly exhibits. Alternatively, spend the afternoon at nearby Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday) for affordable local souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki and enjoy the free Kuhio Beach Hula Show — a free outdoor hula and torch lighting ceremony held Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday evenings at Kuhio Beach Park. A wonderful cultural experience at no cost.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast with grocery store items — yogurt, fruit, and cereal to keep costs low.
meals.lunch: Grab a plate lunch from a food truck near Pearl Harbor or pack your own — budget $10–$12 per person.
meals.dinner: Visit Zippy's Restaurant, a beloved local chain offering affordable Hawaiian comfort food like chili, saimin noodle soup, and plate lunches for $10–$14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed entry passes for the USS Arizona Memorial are free but must be reserved online well in advance — they often book out weeks ahead. The memorial is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays. This is a solemn site; prepare children appropriately.

day_by_day.morning: Take an inter-island flight or ferry to the Big Island (Hawaii Island) — book budget flights on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest in advance for the best rates (typically $60–$100 each way). Alternatively, dedicate this day to exploring more of Oahu if inter-island travel exceeds budget.
day_by_day.afternoon: If on the Big Island, head straight to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park ($35/vehicle, valid for 7 days — great value for families). Stop at the Kilauea Visitor Center to get oriented, then walk the Crater Rim Trail for stunning views of the Kilauea caldera and steam vents.
day_by_day.evening: Drive the Chain of Craters Road at dusk — the lava fields and ocean entry points are dramatic at sunset. Check the park's current volcanic activity updates for any lava viewing opportunities (conditions vary).

meals.breakfast: Early airport breakfast — grab a local pastry or fruit from a terminal café before your flight.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy inside the national park — there are no restaurants within the park, so this is essential for budget travelers.
meals.dinner: Head to Hilo town for dinner at Ken's House of Pancakes, a 24-hour local diner beloved by residents, with meals from $10–$15.

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park is on the Big Island, not Oahu — inter-island travel is required. If staying on Oahu, substitute this day with a visit to Kailua Beach and the Lanikai Pillbox Hike (free). Check volcanic activity status at nps.gov/havo before visiting. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring a jacket — elevation makes it cooler.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park for the Thurston Lava Tube (Nahuku) — a free-to-access (with park entry) walk through a 500-year-old lava tube tunnel. Kids absolutely love this eerie, cave-like experience. Then hike the Devastation Trail, an easy 1-mile boardwalk through a surreal landscape of hardened lava.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Punalu'u Black Sand Beach — one of Hawaii's most unique and photogenic beaches, completely free to visit. Watch endangered Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu) basking on the black sand. Swimming is possible but check conditions. The contrast of black sand, green turtles, and blue ocean is unforgettable.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hilo's waterfront and Farmer's Market (open daily, largest on Wednesday and Saturday) for fresh tropical fruits, local crafts, and affordable snacks. Pick up fresh papaya, star fruit, and coconut for a fraction of supermarket prices.

meals.breakfast: Ken's House of Pancakes in Hilo for a hearty, affordable breakfast — pancakes and eggs for around $10–$12.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and fruit from the Hilo Farmer's Market for a picnic at Punalu'u Black Sand Beach.
meals.dinner: Try Cafe Pesto in Hilo for wood-fired pizzas and local seafood at moderate prices ($14–$18 per dish), or opt for a plate lunch from a local takeout spot for under $12.

day_by_day.notes: Do NOT touch or disturb the sea turtles at Punalu'u — it is illegal under federal law and carries heavy fines. Keep at least 10 feet away. The black sand can get very hot in the sun; bring sandals. August can bring brief rain showers on the Big Island's Hilo side — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akaka Falls State Park near Hilo — a stunning $5/person (or free with Hawaii State Parks pass) short loop trail through lush rainforest leading to the 442-foot Akaka Falls, one of Hawaii's most spectacular waterfalls. The trail is paved and family-friendly, taking about 30–40 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Richardson Ocean Park in Hilo for free snorkeling in a protected cove with excellent visibility and abundant marine life including sea turtles. Bring your own snorkel gear (rented earlier) or borrow from your accommodation. The black lava rock pools are great for kids to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hilo for a relaxed evening. Visit Coconut Island (Moku Ola) — a small island park connected by a footbridge, free to access, with calm swimming areas and beautiful views of Hilo Bay and Mauna Kea.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh fruit and pastries from the Hilo Farmer's Market for a light, affordable breakfast under $8.
meals.lunch: Grab a plate lunch from Puka Puka Kitchen or a similar local spot in Hilo — generous portions of Hawaiian comfort food for $10–$13.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from KTA Super Stores (local Hawaii grocery chain) — fresh fish, rice, and vegetables for a budget-friendly family dinner under $20 total.

day_by_day.notes: Akaka Falls is best visited early morning to avoid tour groups. The trail can be slippery after rain — wear shoes with good grip. Richardson Ocean Park has free parking and restroom facilities. If traveling with young children, the calm waters here are much safer than open ocean beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Take a scenic drive up Saddle Road (Highway 200) toward Mauna Kea — the drive itself through the volcanic landscape is spectacular and free. Stop at the Mauna Kea Visitor Information Station at 9,200 feet elevation for free stargazing programs (offered nightly, weather permitting) and stunning views. Note: summit road requires 4WD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Kona side of the Big Island (about 1.5 hours drive) and visit Kealakekua Bay State Historical Park — snorkel at one of Hawaii's premier snorkeling spots with crystal-clear water and abundant coral. Access via kayak rental ($45–$60/double kayak for 4 hours) or a short hike down to the bay.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kailua-Kona town along Ali'i Drive — browse the open-air shops, watch the sunset over the ocean, and enjoy the lively atmosphere. The waterfront is free to walk and beautiful at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or accommodation breakfast using grocery store supplies — keep it simple with cereal, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Kealakekua Bay — sandwiches, fruit, and plenty of water. No food vendors at the bay itself.
meals.dinner: Try Island Lava Java in Kailua-Kona for casual beachfront dining with burgers, sandwiches, and local dishes at $12–$16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Mauna Kea Visitor Station is at high altitude — some people experience mild altitude sickness. Take it slow, stay hydrated, and descend if you feel unwell. Children under 13 are not recommended at the summit. Kealakekua Bay kayak rentals should be booked in advance during August. Bring plenty of water for the Saddle Road drive — no services for long stretches.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area on the Big Island's Kohala Coast — consistently ranked one of America's best beaches, with free parking ($10 fee) and stunning white sand. The calm, clear water is perfect for family swimming and snorkeling. Arrive early to secure a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Puukohola Heiau National Historic Site — a free national historic site featuring a massive ancient Hawaiian temple (heiau) built by King Kamehameha I. The visitor center offers free ranger-led tours and fascinating insights into Hawaiian history and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Waipio Valley Lookout for a breathtaking free panoramic view of Hawaii's most dramatic valley — steep green cliffs, a black sand beach, and cascading waterfalls. The lookout is accessible by regular car; the valley floor requires 4WD or a guided tour.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the accommodation — pack food to go for a full day on the Kohala Coast.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Hapuna Beach — pack sandwiches, chips, and cold drinks from a grocery store. There is a small snack bar on-site if needed ($8–$12).
meals.dinner: Head to Waimea (Kamuela) town for dinner at Merriman's Market Café or the more budget-friendly Village Burger for local grass-fed beef burgers at $12–$15.

day_by_day.notes: Hapuna Beach can have strong shore break — supervise children closely and heed any posted warning flags. The beach has restrooms, showers, and lifeguards on duty. Puukohola Heiau is a sacred site — treat it with respect and follow all posted guidelines. The Waipio Valley Lookout is a short walk from the parking area and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — return to Oahu if you traveled to the Big Island, or spend a last relaxed morning at your favorite Oahu beach. Visit the Honolulu Museum of Art (free on the last Sunday of the month, otherwise $20/adult, children free) or explore the free Bishop Museum grounds for a final dose of Hawaiian culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Aloha Stadium Swap Meet or Chinatown Honolulu — far more affordable than Waikiki shops. Pick up macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and local crafts at wholesale prices. Explore Chinatown's colorful markets, lei shops, and art galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset at Waikiki Beach — grab a shave ice, watch the sun dip below the horizon, and reflect on an incredible Hawaii adventure. Head to the airport for your departure flight with memories to last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Splurge slightly on a final Hawaiian breakfast — try Eggs 'n Things in Waikiki for famous pancakes with whipped cream and fresh fruit at $12–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Quick and affordable lunch at a local plate lunch spot or food truck — keep it under $12 to stay on budget for the final day.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or a final takeout meal — grab a poke bowl or plate lunch to enjoy before your flight. Many Hawaii airports have local food options beyond typical fast food.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for check-in and security at Honolulu International Airport (HNL), especially during peak August travel season. Use any remaining grocery store snacks for the flight to avoid expensive airport food. Total estimated budget for 10 days (excluding flights and accommodation): $800–$1,200 for a family of 4, depending on inter-island travel choices.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM — no morning activities scheduled. After landing, collect baggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer to accommodation area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Freshen up and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park/Anaheim area to get oriented. Visit a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Easy, low-key first evening — explore Downtown Disney District (free to walk around) or stroll through a nearby outdoor shopping area. Enjoy a relaxed family dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a bite at the airport before or after landing — try a local café or grab-and-go option inside the terminal.
meals.lunch: Pick up a casual meal near the hotel upon arrival — try Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers or In-N-Out Burger on Beach Blvd for a quick, affordable family-friendly option.
meals.dinner: BJ's Restaurant & Brewhouse in Buena Park — family-friendly menu with pizzas, burgers, and salads; mid-range pricing around $15–$25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Since the hotel is in Buena Park, CA (not Hawaii), this itinerary treats Days 1–2 as a California base before flying to Hawaii. Confirm your inter-island or mainland-to-Hawaii flight for Day 3. Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Ensure rental car or transport is arranged in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Knott's Berry Farm in Buena Park — a classic family theme park just minutes from the hotel. Arrive early (10 AM opening) to beat crowds and enjoy rides like GhostRider and Camp Snoopy for younger kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Knott's Berry Farm through the afternoon. Try the famous Boysenberry-themed foods and snacks throughout the park. Take a break at the Calico Mine Ride or watch a live show.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel to pack and prepare for the Hawaii flight tomorrow. Enjoy a relaxed dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby Denny's on Orangethorpe Ave — classic American breakfast for the family, budget-friendly at $8–$14 per person.
meals.lunch: Mrs. Knott's Chicken Dinner Restaurant inside Knott's Berry Farm — iconic fried chicken meals, a California institution; mid-range at $18–$25 per person.
meals.dinner: Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que in Buena Park — hearty BBQ platters, family-friendly atmosphere, mid-range at $16–$28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Knott's Berry Farm tickets online in advance to save money and skip ticket lines. Check the park's schedule for any special August events or shows. Pack light layers as August evenings in Buena Park can be mild. Confirm Hawaii flight details and set early alarms if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Buena Park early for LAX or John Wayne Airport (SNA) for your flight to Honolulu, Oahu. Upon arrival in Honolulu, collect bags and pick up rental car. Drive to your Oahu accommodation and check in.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, head to Waikiki Beach for a gentle first introduction to Hawaii's iconic shoreline. Let the kids splash in the calm, warm waters. Rent a boogie board from a beachside vendor ($10–$15/hour) for some easy family fun.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Kalakaua Avenue in Waikiki — browse local shops, watch street performers, and soak in the vibrant Hawaiian atmosphere as the sun sets over the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or airport café before departure — keep it simple with pastries and coffee.
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In near Kapahulu Ave, Honolulu — a beloved local institution serving classic Hawaiian plate lunches; very affordable at $10–$14 per person.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki at the Outrigger Waikiki Beach Resort — oceanfront dining with Hawaiian-inspired dishes like huli huli chicken and fresh fish; mid-range at $20–$35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: August weather in Hawaii averages highs around 17°C (low-to-mid 80s°F) with occasional rain showers — pack a light rain jacket. Book your Oahu accommodation in advance; mid-range options in Waikiki like the Aston Waikiki Beach Hotel or Courtyard Marriott Waikiki Beach run $180–$250/night. Confirm rental car reservation before landing.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. Arrive early (7:00–7:30 AM) as the bay fills up quickly and has a daily visitor cap. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel among hundreds of colorful tropical fish in crystal-clear waters. Equipment rental available on-site ($12–$15).
day_by_day.afternoon: After Hanauma Bay, drive the scenic Makapu'u Point Lighthouse Trail (2.5-mile round trip, paved, family-friendly) for stunning coastal views. Then stop at Lanikai Beach for a quieter, postcard-perfect beach experience with calm turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Waikiki. Stop at the Kaimuki neighborhood for dinner — one of Honolulu's best local dining districts with authentic, non-touristy options.

meals.breakfast: Grab malasadas (Portuguese donuts) from Leonard's Bakery on Kapahulu Ave — a Hawaii institution; budget-friendly at $1.50–$2 each. Pair with coffee from a nearby café.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch — pick up poke bowls from Foodland Farms or a local grocery store near Hanauma Bay before heading out; fresh, affordable, and perfect for a beach day ($10–$15 per person).
meals.dinner: Koko Head Café in Kaimuki — beloved local brunch-and-dinner spot with creative Hawaiian-inspired dishes; mid-range at $16–$24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online — book at least 2–3 days ahead as slots sell out fast. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only (required by Hawaii law). Bring water shoes as the reef entry can be rocky. The Makapu'u trail is stroller-accessible but can be warm — bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures (Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori). The center opens at 11:45 AM; arrive early to explore the village exhibits, canoe rides, and cultural demonstrations at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Polynesian Cultural Center — catch the afternoon canoe pageant on the lagoon (typically around 2:30 PM), a spectacular free-floating parade of performers in traditional costumes. Let kids try hands-on activities like coconut husking, spear throwing, and hula lessons.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a breathtaking theatrical production featuring fire dancing, acrobatics, and traditional music. Dinner package included with most ticket bundles.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab açaí bowls from Lanikai Juice in Kailua on the drive up to the North Shore — fresh, healthy, and delicious; $10–$14 per person.
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — all-you-can-eat Hawaiian and Polynesian cuisine included in the Ambassador package; excellent value for families.
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau Dinner or Gateway Buffet dinner included with the evening show package at the Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional Hawaiian foods like kalua pig, poi, and haupia dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets online in advance — the Ambassador Package ($120–$140/adult, $90–$110/child) includes the buffet, all village access, and the evening show, making it excellent value. The drive from Waikiki is about 1 hour via H-3 or the scenic Pali Highway. Allow a full day (11 AM–9 PM). The center is run by Brigham Young University–Hawaii and is family-friendly and alcohol-free.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots. Start at Ono Hawaiian Foods in Kaimuki for laulau (pork wrapped in taro leaves), poi, and lomi salmon. Then head to Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award winner) for pipikaula short ribs and squid luau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum — Hawaii's premier natural and cultural history museum. Explore the Hawaiian Hall with its stunning featherwork capes and royal artifacts, the Science Adventure Center (great for kids), and the planetarium. Budget about 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ala Moana Center — Hawaii's largest open-air shopping mall — for some souvenir shopping and people-watching. Enjoy sunset views from the adjacent Ala Moana Beach Park.

meals.breakfast: Café Kaila in Market City Shopping Center — known as one of Honolulu's best breakfast spots with fluffy pancakes and eggs Benedict; mid-range at $14–$20 per person.
meals.lunch: The plate lunch food tour IS lunch — budget $12–$18 per person across 2–3 stops for a generous, authentic Hawaiian meal experience.
meals.dinner: Mariposa at Neiman Marcus in Ala Moana — elegant but accessible lunch/dinner with beautiful views and Hawaiian-inspired cuisine; mid-range at $22–$35 per person. Alternatively, try the Ala Moana Food Court for a more budget-friendly option with diverse local vendors.

day_by_day.notes: Helena's Hawaiian Food is closed on weekends — Friday is the perfect day to visit. Arrive early as lines form quickly. The Bishop Museum admission is $25–$30/adult and $18–$22/child — check for family bundle discounts. The plate lunch food tour works best in the late morning (10 AM–12 PM) before the lunch rush. Keep a cooler in the car if you want to save any leftovers.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) — short inter-island flight (approximately 30 minutes). Book with Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest for $60–$100/person. Pick up rental car at Kahului Airport and drive to your Maui accommodation (mid-range options in Kihei or Lahaina area, $180–$260/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — arrive at one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand along West Maui. Set up at the central beach area near Whalers Village. Swim in the calm, warm waters, build sandcastles, and enjoy the stunning views of Lanai and Molokai on the horizon.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at the north end of Kaanapali Beach — a local diver leaps from the lava rock at sunset carrying a torch, a nightly tradition. Browse Whalers Village outdoor mall for shopping and dining.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Kahului Airport or a quick stop at Maui's Whole Foods Market in Kahului — fresh fruit, pastries, and local items to fuel the travel morning.
meals.lunch: Hula Grill Kaanapali on the beach — open-air barefoot bar and grill with fresh fish tacos, burgers, and salads right on the sand; mid-range at $16–$26 per person.
meals.dinner: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman in Whalers Village — farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine with wood-fired pizzas, fresh fish, and excellent cocktails; mid-range at $20–$35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights at least 2–3 weeks in advance for best prices. Kaanapali Beach has free public beach access — paid parking is available at Whalers Village (validated with purchase). The cliff diving ceremony happens nightly at sunset — arrive 15 minutes early for a good viewing spot. Apply reef-safe sunscreen and bring beach umbrellas as August sun is strong.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Road to Hana — one of the world's most scenic coastal drives (approximately 52 miles, 2.5–3 hours one way). Stop at Twin Falls for an easy family hike to beautiful waterfalls, then continue to the Garden of Eden Arboretum for lush tropical scenery and ocean overlooks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the Road to Hana — stop at Wai'anapanapa State Park to see the dramatic black sand beach and sea caves (advance reservations required, $5/person entry fee). Arrive in Hana town for a brief exploration of this charming, remote community.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive back toward Kaanapali/Kihei (allow 2.5–3 hours). Stop at a roadside stand for fresh fruit and snacks. Arrive back at accommodation for a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing — aim to leave by 7:30–8:00 AM to beat traffic on the Road to Hana.
meals.lunch: Roadside food trucks and stands along the Road to Hana — try fresh coconut, banana bread from Aunty Sandy's in Ke'anae ($3–$5/loaf), and plate lunches from local vendors; budget $10–$15 per person.
meals.dinner: Nalu's South Shore Grill in Kihei — casual, family-friendly Hawaiian comfort food with generous portions; mid-range at $14–$22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana requires advance parking reservations at Wai'anapanapa State Park — book at hawaiistateparks.reserveamerica.com. Start early to avoid traffic and afternoon rain showers. Bring motion sickness remedies for kids as the road has 620 curves and 59 bridges. Pack a cooler with drinks and snacks. The full round trip is a long day — consider turning back at Wai'anapanapa if the family is tired.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Kahului, Maui (OGG) to Kona or Hilo, Big Island (KOA or ITO) — short inter-island flight (30–45 minutes). Pick up rental car and drive toward Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (approximately 45 minutes from Hilo, 2.5 hours from Kona). Check in to accommodation near Volcano Village or Hilo ($150–$220/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Drive the 11-mile Crater Rim Drive to overlook Kilauea Caldera and the Halema'uma'u Crater. Walk the Devastation Trail (0.4 miles, paved, family-friendly) through a surreal landscape of hardened lava and recovering vegetation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Kilauea Overlook after dark — if lava is actively glowing (check NPS website for current activity), the nighttime view of the crater is absolutely spectacular and unforgettable for the whole family. Check the NPS Hawaii Volcanoes website for current eruption status.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Kahului Airport or hotel before the flight — grab pastries and fruit to go.
meals.lunch: Cafe Ono at the Volcano Art Center inside the national park — sandwiches, soups, and local snacks in a beautiful setting; mid-range at $12–$18 per person.
meals.dinner: Thai Thai Restaurant in Volcano Village — a beloved local gem just outside the park with authentic Thai cuisine and generous portions; budget-friendly at $12–$20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park entry fee is $35/vehicle (valid for 7 days) — worth every penny. Check the NPS website (nps.gov/havo) for current eruption activity and any trail closures before visiting. Bring warm layers as Volcano Village sits at 4,000 feet elevation and can be cool and misty even in August. The park is open 24 hours — the evening lava glow viewing is a highlight not to miss.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — visit the Thurston Lava Tube (Nahuku) inside Hawaii Volcanoes National Park for a short, easy walk through a 500-year-old lava tube tunnel (free with park admission, family-friendly). Then drive to the Chain of Craters Road for sweeping views of ancient lava flows meeting the Pacific Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kona (approximately 2.5 hours) for departure preparations. Stop at a Kona coffee farm along the way — many offer free or low-cost tours and tastings. Browse the Kona waterfront for last-minute souvenirs at the Kona Inn Shopping Village.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Kona International Airport (KOA) for your return flight to the mainland. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaii adventure filled with beaches, culture, volcanoes, and family memories.

meals.breakfast: Kilauea Lodge Restaurant in Volcano Village — charming lodge dining with hearty breakfasts including eggs, local fruit, and fresh-baked bread; mid-range at $14–$20 per person.
meals.lunch: Island Lava Java in Kona — casual oceanfront café with sandwiches, salads, and excellent Kona coffee; mid-range at $13–$19 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or early dinner at Jackie Rey's Ohana Grill in Kona — family-friendly Hawaiian fusion with fresh fish and local ingredients; mid-range at $18–$30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight times and allow at least 2 hours before departure at Kona Airport. Return rental car with a full tank to avoid fuel surcharges. Pack any liquid souvenirs (Kona coffee, macadamia nut oils) in checked luggage. Agricultural inspection is required when leaving Hawaii — dispose of any fresh fruits or plants before boarding. Consider shipping larger souvenir purchases home to avoid baggage fees.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 AM — Flight Alaska lands. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to hotel. Check-in at SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park (note: this is a staging night near Anaheim before flying to Hawaii). Freshen up and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Anaheim area at a leisurely pace. Visit Downtown Disney District for premium shopping and a relaxed stroll — no park ticket required. Browse luxury boutiques and enjoy the atmosphere as a gentle introduction to the vacation.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a refined dinner at a nearby upscale restaurant to recover from travel. Early night to prepare for the Hawaii-bound flight the next morning.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal or airport lounge dining at departure airport
meals.lunch: Light bites at the hotel or a nearby café upon arrival — try Umami Burger or a quality local spot in Buena Park
meals.dinner: Napa Rose at Disney's Grand Californian Hotel (approx. 10 min drive) — award-winning California cuisine in an elegant Arts & Crafts setting

day_by_day.notes: The hotel address is in Buena Park, CA — this appears to be a pre-Hawaii staging night. Confirm inter-island or mainland-to-Hawaii flight for Day 2. Keep luggage organized for early departure. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Early checkout and private luxury transfer to LAX or John Wayne Airport. Board flight to Honolulu, Oahu (approximately 5–6 hours). Arrive and check into a luxury Waikiki resort such as The Royal Hawaiian or Halekulani Hotel. Enjoy welcome amenities and ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: First taste of Hawaii — take a leisurely walk along Waikiki Beach. Rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas through the resort. Dip your toes in the warm Pacific and soak in the iconic Diamond Head backdrop. Light snorkeling directly off Waikiki Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's oceanfront bar. Watch the famous Waikiki sunset with a mai tai in hand before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Airport lounge breakfast or in-flight premium dining
meals.lunch: La Mer or Orchids at Halekulani — refined Pacific Rim cuisine with ocean views
meals.dinner: House Without a Key at Halekulani — iconic open-air beachfront dining with live Hawaiian music and hula performance under a century-old kiawe tree

day_by_day.notes: Book luxury resort well in advance — The Royal Hawaiian ('Pink Palace of the Pacific') and Halekulani are top-tier Waikiki options. Request an ocean-view room or suite. Confirm airport transfer with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — depart early (7:00–7:30 AM) to secure entry as daily visitor numbers are capped. This UNESCO-protected marine sanctuary offers crystal-clear waters teeming with sea turtles, parrotfish, and hundreds of tropical species. Private guided snorkel tour recommended for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Waikiki and enjoy the resort pool and beach. Optional: book a private outrigger canoe experience along the Waikiki shoreline — a quintessential Hawaiian family activity. Kids and adults alike will love paddling with a local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Kahala neighborhood. Visit Kahala Mall for premium shopping, then head to dinner at one of Honolulu's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — buffet or à la carte at the hotel restaurant to fuel the morning snorkel
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch boxes prepared by the resort or a stop at Kona Brewing Company Hawaii for fresh seafood and craft beverages
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia Waikiki — Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto's stunning oceanfront restaurant featuring innovative Asian-Pacific cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance online reservations — book at least 2 days ahead. Entry fee applies. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only (Hawaii law). Water temperature is warm (~26°C) and ideal for families.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — depart by 9:00 AM for the 35-mile drive to Laie on Oahu's North Shore. Spend the morning exploring six authentic Polynesian village exhibits representing Hawaii, Samoa, Aotearoa (New Zealand), Fiji, Tahiti, and Tonga. Engage in hands-on cultural activities like fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' canoe pageant on the lagoon (afternoon show). Explore the IMAX theater and additional cultural demonstrations. This is a full-day immersive family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — a premium all-you-can-eat Hawaiian feast with live entertainment, fire knife dancing, and traditional hula. One of the most celebrated luau experiences in all of Hawaii.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with premium package tickets featuring Hawaiian and Polynesian dishes
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau dinner included with the evening luau package — traditional imu-roasted kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, haupia, and more

day_by_day.notes: Book the Polynesian Cultural Center's 'Ambassador Package' for the best experience — includes priority seating, guided tours, and luau access. The center is closed on Sundays. Drive along the scenic Kamehameha Highway on the return for beautiful coastal views.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — join a guided premium food tour of Honolulu's most iconic local eateries. Visit legendary spots serving classic plate lunches: two scoops of rice, macaroni salad, and your choice of kalua pork, chicken katsu, or loco moco. Explore Chinatown's vibrant food markets and sample shave ice at a celebrated local institution.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial — a deeply moving and historically significant experience for the whole family. Tour the USS Arizona Memorial, USS Missouri Battleship, and the Pacific Aviation Museum. Book a premium guided tour for in-depth storytelling.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki for a relaxed evening. Stroll the Kalakaua Avenue luxury shopping strip — Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Tiffany & Co. are all represented. Enjoy a nightcap at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Café Kaila in Market City — beloved local breakfast spot known for creative eggs Benedict and fresh fruit plates
meals.lunch: Plate lunch food tour covers multiple tastings — Helena's Hawaiian Food (James Beard Award winner) is a must-stop
meals.dinner: Alan Wong's Honolulu — legendary farm-to-table Hawaiian Regional Cuisine by one of Hawaii's most celebrated chefs; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor requires advance reservations for the USS Arizona Memorial (free but timed entry). Arrive early as it gets busy. The food tour is best booked through a local premium operator. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight from Honolulu to Maui (approximately 30 minutes). Check into a luxury Kaanapali resort — the Four Seasons Resort Maui at Wailea or Hyatt Regency Maui are exceptional choices. Settle in and enjoy the resort's world-class amenities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — spend the afternoon on one of America's most celebrated beaches. Nearly three miles of golden sand, calm turquoise waters, and stunning views of Lanai and Molokai. Rent premium snorkel gear and explore the famous Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) — a sacred Hawaiian site and excellent snorkel spot teeming with marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a nightly tradition where a torch-lighter dives from the lava rock into the ocean. Watch from the beach with a cocktail in hand.

meals.breakfast: In-flight snack or quick bite at Honolulu Airport's premium lounge
meals.lunch: Leilani's on the Beach, Kaanapali — casual-upscale oceanfront dining with fresh fish tacos, seared ahi, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Japengo at Hyatt Regency Maui — Pacific Rim cuisine with sushi, fresh local fish, and panoramic ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights on Hawaiian Airlines for the best experience. Kaanapali Beach is on Maui's west coast — most luxury resorts are directly beachfront. The water is calm and ideal for families. August weather on Maui's leeward coast is typically sunny and dry.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana — embark on one of the world's most scenic drives. Hire a private luxury van with a knowledgeable local guide for the family. Stop at Twin Falls, Garden of Eden Arboretum, Wailua Falls, and the black sand beach at Wai'anapanapa State Park. The lush rainforest scenery is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana journey — visit the sacred Pools of 'Ohe'o (Seven Sacred Pools) in Haleakalā National Park. Swim in the natural freshwater pools surrounded by bamboo forest and waterfalls. A truly magical family experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Kaanapali (approximately 2.5–3 hours with guide). Arrive back at the resort for a relaxing evening. Optional: resort spa treatment to unwind after the day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — fuel up for the long scenic drive
meals.lunch: Roadside stops along Hana Highway — fresh banana bread from Aunty Sandy's (a legendary Hana tradition), tropical fruit stands, and packed gourmet picnic from the resort
meals.dinner: Merriman's Maui in Kapalua — farm-to-table pioneer Peter Merriman's stunning oceanfront restaurant; sunset views are spectacular

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 64 miles with 620 curves and 59 bridges — a private guided tour is strongly recommended for families. Start early (7:00 AM) to beat crowds. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations. Bring swimwear, water shoes, and reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakalā Sunrise Experience — wake at 2:30 AM for a private luxury guided tour to the summit of Haleakalā volcano (10,023 ft). Watch the sunrise above the clouds from the crater rim — a profoundly spiritual and visually stunning experience. Bring warm layers as summit temperatures can drop to 5–10°C.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by midday. Rest and recover at the resort pool or beach. Optional: book a family surf lesson at Kaanapali Beach with a certified instructor — beginner-friendly waves make this ideal for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Premium sunset dinner cruise along the Maui coastline. Sail aboard a luxury catamaran with gourmet catering, open bar, live Hawaiian music, and stunning views of the West Maui Mountains and neighboring islands.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast provided by the tour operator at the Haleakalā summit — hot coffee, pastries, and fruit
meals.lunch: Resort poolside dining — fresh poke bowls, grilled fish, and tropical smoothies
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner cruise — gourmet catering featuring fresh Hawaiian seafood, prime cuts, and tropical desserts aboard a luxury catamaran

day_by_day.notes: Haleakalā sunrise requires a timed entry reservation through recreation.gov — book months in advance as spots fill quickly. The summit is cold and windy; pack jackets and layers for the whole family. The afternoon is intentionally light to recover from the very early morning.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight from Maui to the Big Island (Hawaii Island) — approximately 45 minutes. Check into a luxury resort on the Kohala Coast — the Four Seasons Resort Hualalai or Mauna Kea Beach Hotel are iconic choices. Enjoy the resort's pristine private beach and world-class facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — drive approximately 1.5 hours to the park (or arrange a private helicopter tour for a premium aerial perspective). Witness the raw power of Kīlauea, one of the world's most active volcanoes. Walk the Crater Rim Trail, explore lava tubes at Thurston Lava Tube, and see the dramatic Halema'uma'u Crater.
day_by_day.evening: If lava is flowing to the ocean (check current conditions), arrange a private lava boat tour for a once-in-a-lifetime experience viewing molten lava entering the sea at night — an extraordinary spectacle.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or airport lounge before departure
meals.lunch: Volcano House Restaurant inside Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — historic lodge dining with crater views; try the Big Island beef burger or fresh catch
meals.dinner: CanoeHouse at Mauna Lani — one of Hawaii's most celebrated restaurants featuring locally sourced Hawaiian Regional Cuisine with oceanfront ambiance and live music

day_by_day.notes: Check USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current volcanic activity before visiting. The park is open 24 hours and lava viewing is most dramatic after dark. Wear closed-toe shoes and long pants for lava field walking. Helicopter tours over the volcano are available from Hilo or Kona airports — book in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast and last swim at the private beach. Visit the stunning Mauna Kea Beach for a final snorkel session — the calm, clear waters here are home to sea turtles, manta rays, and vibrant reef fish. A perfect farewell to Hawaii's ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure preparation — checkout and private luxury transfer to Kona International Airport (KOA). Browse the airport's local shops for premium Hawaiian souvenirs: Kona coffee, macadamia nut chocolates, and locally made crafts. Board inter-island or direct mainland flight.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or upon return — reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Hawaiian journey spanning Oahu, Maui, and the Big Island.

meals.breakfast: Grand resort farewell breakfast — full à la carte spread with fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Island Lava Java in Kailua-Kona — beloved local café near the airport for a final taste of Big Island flavors: fresh fish tacos, acai bowls, and world-famous Kona coffee
meals.dinner: In-flight premium dining or airport restaurant upon return

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for airport check-in on the Big Island. Purchase authentic 100% Kona coffee directly from local farms or the airport — avoid blends. Consider shipping any large purchases home through the hotel concierge. Keep one carry-on bag accessible for any fragile or valuable souvenirs.
